Have healthy habits like going to the gym, eating well, meditating, letting go, building your business or career, anything that reminds you thst she’s the cherry on top of the cake but not the whole cake. Name: Daniel Subke
Question: Is there anything wrong with going back to your ex?
Answer: There are many things wrong with it. People usually don’t change and will stick to the behavioral patterns they‘re used to They only change those behaviors when they want to or when they hit rock bottom really hard. That’s why you can improve and heal yourself all you want but never really have an ex feel about and behave towards you the way you want them to feel and behave. It‘s because this kind of change is beyond your influence and control. Because they got so used to this old version of you that they refuse to acknowledge and see the new, improved and healed version of you. Because acknowledging the new you means they would have to change their behaviors and out of fear of change or pride and ego, they just wont do that. Now that’s not to say it‘s impossible to have a more stable and improved relationship with an ex after a reconciliation. It just means that getting this result is extraordinarily unlikely because, again, people usually don’t change, especially not if they think they don’t need to. This is also why chasing an ex is a shit strategy that never works — you’ll constantly be met with rejection, fierce resistance and they’ll always give you the impression that you’re never good enough for them. When in reality, you’re already and always have been good enough. Unless both of you improved each others behaviors that contributed to the breakup, you’ll only repeat the past all over again And even if both of you improved each others behaviors that contributed to the breakup, there’s no guarantee that the new versions of both of you have the deeper alignment that’s necessary for a reconciliation to be a whole lot better and more stable than the first try. So, when reconciling with an ex, always keep in mind that if you do it with the intent to re-create what you had going on in the past, you will break up again fairly soon because the way it was has led both of you to the first breakup, and it will create a second breakup for the same reasons as before. The only way for such a reconciliation to turn into something drastically better is to change in the same or similar direction, to fundamentally change the way you approach each other and learn from past mistakes rather than repeating them. Also, this willingness to change the approach has to be mutual. What feels safe and familiar isn’t always good for us Seeing your ex again, holding them in your arms and experiencing intimacy with them may feel insanely good because due to the emotional attachment to them, it’s what’s most familiar to you and what feels the safest. But this doesn’t automatically mean you’re good for each other. Especially not if they don’t give you any respect or are very manipulative. In fact, if the only reason you want them back is because you fear change and solitude, if being together causes you to not grow as a person or even to evolve backwards, then you’re clearly not good for each other. Because couples who are good for each other help each other to heal, grow and evolve.

Question: Why is reciprocation important on relationships?
Answer: Because just like a business can’t exist without money, a relationship can’t exist without reciprocity. In other words, if there’s an extremely unequal level of reciprocation or none at all, you don’t have a real relationship. You‘re just being used for attention and validation or use others for this. That’s why this strategy of chasing and wanting to be chased all the time without ever initiating sucks and never works. It‘s also why a lack of reciprocation must never be tolerated for longer than necessary. If people want a relationship, they need to be willing to open themselves up to true intimacy. They need to give to each other, because it‘s only through mutual giving that the needs of both are being met. Otherwise things will never progress. And if the person you‘re dealing with (be it your ex or someone you feel attracted to) just wont reciprocate despite your best efforts, you owe it to yourself to dump them and instead choose people who choose you.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: What are the reasons behind some men having difficulties with being alone? Is it due to a need for companionship or a fear of being alone?
Answer: As stated well in another answer by Tom Nault, it‘s definitely not just men. This is a collective problem that’s affecting a lot of people, both men and women in this world. Anyway, here are my two cents on this, some reasons why many have difficulties with solitude (and why I also used to struggle with it for a long time): They have never been single for long in their life In fact, I have observed in myself and in the people around me, in family, friends, acquaintances, coworkers, clients, etc. that most of them never stayed single for longer than 6 months to a year and usually jumped into a new relationship fairly quickly after their divorce or breakups (those new relationships either lasted many years or are still going strong as of today). What I also observed consistently is that most of them were terrified of the mere thought of being single to the point where they got panic attacks and stuff like that. The reason for that was because they simply got too used to having a girlfriend/boyfriend/wife/husband and never really gave themselves the chance to experience what real solitude is like and how to actually enjoy it Because unfortunately, there’s still a lot of stigma around singlehood and solitude. And quiet frankly, it‘s definitely not easy to learn to enjoy solitude when you’ve been in a relationship for most, if not all your life as this is a drastic change of lifestyle. This is also why I don’t blame people for trying to escape solitude after breakups and choosing to do a rebound relationship instead, even if it‘s not healthy. Life is about relationships In fact, we all have an innate and fundamental need for belonging, connection, socializing and stuff like that. We cannot possibly un-need this need either. This is why all of us have an innate aversion to and fear of solitude. We don’t really want to be all on our own forever with no connection or relationship whatsoever. And neither are we meant to. So, that’s why it‘s natural to be afraid of solitude at first. The key is to improve the relationship with yourself I haven‘t been in a strong romantic relationship since around 2018/2019. But I don’t really feel ashamed of this anymore. Neither do I dread the idea of solitude. Sure, I do occasionally long for a relationship but, it‘s not so bad anymore. But, I learned to love solitude during those 5 years by focusing on improving the relationship with myself and refusing to give in to the pressure of needing to be in a long-term relationship, even if everyone around me has one. In fact, right now I‘m the only man in my whole family with no kids and who‘s never been married. But again, I‘m cool with that. Because I have built and am still building a solid foundation — a good relationship with myself. This relationship is what colors and shapes the quality of every other relationship I will have. Because how can I possibly be happy in a relationship if I can’t be happy with who I am? How can I add value to a womans life if I can’t add value to my own? How can I expect to be loved and wanted by a woman if I don’t want and love myself? If I can’t tolerate, heal and enjoy my own presence, my emotional/psychological wounds, my thoughts, my emotions, my insecurities, my fears? In my book, everyone must focus on building this solid foundation first if their intention is to have an amazing relationship with someone else. Because what is there to fear about being in solitude when you have genuine inner peace? When you focus on that, solitude becomes like an adventure you will slowly start enjoying and get used to. There will be a sense of peace, groundedness and self-confidence that emanates from you which others find very attractive — and which may attract the men/women you can build relationships with that last a very long time.

Question: What advice would you give your 23 year old self today?
Answer: As of today, I’m 32 and this is what I would say: Your twenties are supposed to be difficult, challenging and filled with adversity They’re a transformative decade in our life that mature, grow and change us. They mark the end of immaturity and initiate the transition into full adulthood where life will equip you with the tools, resilience and skills needed to navigate through life successfully. However, this won’t be easy. In fact, you’ll be alone most of the time. It will suck, get pretty dark and painful and there will most likely be more setbacks, disappointments and heartbreaks than successes and joy. But, if you keep cultivating an open mind and a growth mindset, you will come out on the good end. You’ll eventually get used to it and manage to power through somehow.  Think about what kind of man you want to be Because a lot of the decisions you make in your twenties will either make you better or bitter in your thirties and beyond. They will shape your personality and what kind of man you’re becoming. So, do you want to be an honest man others can trust or a dishonest man others will avoid? Do you want to be a man with humility, who can introspect and grow or a man with too much pride and arrogance who doesn’t introspect nor grow? Do you want to be a man of integrity and substance or an unreliable man whose word doesn’t mean anything? Do you want to be a man women want or do you want to be a man who hates them because no woman wants him? Do you want to enjoy the bliss of financial freedom/stability or do you want to financially depend on your parents/friends/girlfriends/boyfriends, having to ask them for money all the time? What kind of man you become depends on the decisions you make throughout your twenties. Therefore, do your best to make wise, well-informed decisions that are based on logic, reason and truth a lot more than on feelings and emotions. Seek out advice, insights and guidance from those who are ahead of you a few steps, with more experience than you in whatever area you need help with. This applies to all aspects of your life. Be it relationships/dating, career, personal growth, health, etc. You won’t always be able to make good and wise decisions but, this is okay because eventually you’ll learn from it.  It’s okay to fail Throughout my twenties, I have failed all the time. However, it weren’t for these failures, I wouldn’t have the stability and security that I have now. I wouldn’t be as self-confident as I am today had I never made certain mistakes in my twenties that eventually redirected me to a much better path and which helped me to improve myself. Therefore, don’t allow a fear of failure to hold you back from taking action.  There will be many things you’ll have to let go of and say goodbye to Many of those things will be certain relationships, perspectives, habits, ways of thinking, ways of carrying you...

Instead, take your power back by realizing that closure is an illusion and that you really don’t need it to heal. Question: How do I know if no contact is working?
Answer: All the following assumes you‘re the dumpee who went no contact on the dumper. The clearest sign that no contact is working for you, that you‘re healing, improving and growing and that you’ve been doing all the right things is when your ex starts coming back around and reaching out to you again when you least expect it and don’t even want, let alone think about it anymore. When they check to see how life has been for you, either online or in person. Usually, this takes around 3–6 months to a year of complete silence and focus on personal growth depending on how deep and meaningful the relationship was to your dumper ex. It takes this long because right after the breakup and shortly before it, most dumper exes put you in a box. They will view you as emotionally weak, undesirable and needy and they will also expect you to consistently chase after them, to break no contact and always come back around. Now when this doesn’t happen, when you broke these patterns, when you don’t do what they expect you to do because you finally managed to put your own well-being first, to let go, heal and improve and rediscover life without them, to walk away and mean it, they start to panic and get anxious. They can intuitively and energetically sense you disconnecting, moving on and slipping away for real this time. Because they don’t want that since they need the reassurance that you need them more than they need you in order for themselves to be and feel self-confident, they will come back around. However, very often their intentions behind this aren’t genuine and mostly of egocentric nature. What they really want is for you to undo your healing, to slip back into old unwanted patterns where you chase again so that they can feel like they still have full power and control over you. As soon as this happens, you‘re essentially back at square one. And that’s why when they do come back around, you got to be firm with the NC boundary and not immediately forgive or take them back. During those moments, you got to remind yourself of all the shit your ex put you through, of why you had to go NC in the first place. These moments are a trap and kind of a test from the universe. It‘s asking you: 'Do you really want this?' 'Did you really change and improve or are you jsut faking it?' 'Have you really learned your lessons or not?'

Question: What is character assassination and how does it protect narcissists for being held accountable for their abuse? How does it affect the victim?
Answer: It‘s when the narcissist tries everything to make others perceive you in a very negative light to ruin your reputation and thus further isolate you so that you are easier to control, manipulate and abuse. They do this by spreading malicious gossip and lies about you behind your back, by twisting the truth, accusing you of doing everything they themselves are doing so that nobody suspects that they’re the crazy psycho narcissist they accuse you of being. Those who blindly believe everything the narcissist says about you are flying monkeys (essentially the narcissists slaves and blind supporters). More often than not, those are people who either don’t know about narcissism or who love drama, who are very naive, gullible and easy to manipulate. And this is how they dodge accountability for their abuse. They try to 'recruit' as many flying monkeys as they can to use them as a shield, so that the truth never comes out. Which it eventually and inevitably will at some point. It‘s just a matter of time. And when it does come out, when some of their flying monkeys wake up to the truth, add one and one together and realize that the bullshit they‘ve been told about you by the narcissist doesn’t add up, a few things are likely to happen: As for how it affects those on the receiving end of the character assasination, it‘s often that they end up believing that they really are the narcissist (which isn’t true), that their reputation gets ruined almost to the point beyond repair, that their self-confidence is shattered or that they lose significant relationships, friendships and connections in their life. So, a narcissists character assasination is no joke. It can destroy lifes and ruin otherwise amazing relationships.

Question: I rejected him and he started ignoring me but I like him and I gave him so many hints that I like him too, but he is still not doing anything about it. Why?

Question: What should I do if I'm scared of the future?
Answer: I‘ve experienced this myself several times but managed to overcome it by realizing this: The future isn’t real, nor is your past Both are really a mental projection, a story that you habitually picture and play out in your mind. A story about everything that can go wrong. The result of this is that it produces more fear, because you keep thinking of worst case scenarios that probably will never happen. In fact, I don’t remember a time in my life where my imagined worst case scenarios became a reality, and I used to picture worst case scenarios for a long time. And if they did become a reality, it was never as bad or as horrible as I thought. Sure, it was painful and sucked but eventually, in the end I always found and created a way through such setbacks and adversities somehow and came out on the good end every single time. And the way I did this, the way I managed to let go of and transcend this fear of the future was by creating: I created a vision of what I wanted my life to be like. I wrote down a couple of long-term goals that were really meaningful and steps to get there. Creating inner alignment, then taking action and achieving those goals ended up massively improving my life and also helped me transcend this fear. So, realize that even if things go wrong, you can and will find a way through this somehow when it happens. Also that it’s okay to be afraid of the future, because it‘s showing you that you care about yourself and your life. It‘s showing you that you want to be secure (financially, emotionally, physically, romantically, etc.) and that you don’t want to be stuck in fear all the time. It‘s a way how your soul/higher self/god/the universe/whatever higher power you believe in inspires you to take action and create the reality you want.

Question: Is being a simp bad?
Answer: I’ll first define and explain what being a male simp really means. As a man, you’re not a simp if you love your girlfriend. So, being a simp is not just bad, it’s catastrophically fatal because it will get you manipulated, cheated on, keep women away from you and quickly destroy not just your self-confidence and self-respect but, also your life in general. The cure to this is to build self-respect. To no longer forgive cheating. To stop making excuses for her dysfunctional or abusive behavior. To stop idealizing and chasing after a girl who doesn’t want you, who doesn’t reciprocate. To always be in a position to walk away. To learn to say no and hold her accountable for stepping over the line. And of course to have boundaries, a certain level of standards that you expect from a relationship.

Question: She tells me she loves me , but she's in a codependent relationship, she told me many times that she hates her boyfriend but just can't get out of the relationship, should I just let her go (we're 100% soul mates)?
Answer: I‘ll be your voice of reason and help you become more conscious and aware by saying that she doesn’t love you. She‘s playing you. She‘s using your kindness, willingness to love and goodwill against you. Why? Only she knows for sure but generally speaking, people who are already in a relationship do that because they need attention which they currently don’t get in their relationship. At first you may think that there’s no real problem with this, that you‘re a lot better than her current man and that it’s only a matter of time until she leaves him for you. However, the blindspot in this is that she doesn’t really respect or view you as an equal. That she‘s operating from a place of fear, not love. That she’s emotionally cheating with you (and will most likely cheat on you in case you do end up together). That she’s using you as a backup-option which she only goes to when her relationship goes south. Such situations usually don’t well. It will eventually get you caught up in a toxic on-off cycle where you get sucked into the drama of her current relationship. Where she stays with you for a while but then break up to go back to her ex. Where at some point you‘ll be so emotionally jaded and drained that you‘ll feel destroyed because there’s no real stability there but only confusion, unrequited love and pain. Anyway, the question I want you to ask yourself is: Do you really want this? Do you really want to be with a woman who deals with problems in a relationship through escapism, avoidance and cheating rather than solving them through authenticity, honesty and truth? I know it’s not easy to see this clearly or even to accept it because right now you’re deeply infatuated and most likely idealize her because you feel really good in her presence. You may even have daydreamed about an amazing future with her. But, this is an illusion. It‘s like a spell she casted on you that makes you a willingness puppet. In order to remove this spell, regain your power and make the right decision for yourself, you got to approach this with wisdom and rationale and put your feelings on the backburner for a while. Because the short-term pleasure and relief you get from being with her isn’t worth the long-term pain that this on-off situation and drama (which btw isn’t yours) will bring into your life. So, here’s how I recommend you proceed from here to protect your heart and inner peace: Why do I recommend this? Because you owe yourself the right to be loved the right way. Because you‘ll always be giving 100% while she‘s only giving 30% at best. Also because relationships dynamics where your bf/gf is still in an unclear, open-ended and complicated situation with their ex suck and aren’t healthy. Hope this helps.

Question: Why is it too bad to talk about my goals?

They will throw doubt your way, make fun of it and tell you you won’t make it. So, don’t share your goals with just anyone, because this world has some really fucked up people, people who don’t want to see you suceed and win at life. Instead, let your results speak for themselves. Drown them with your results and they will quickly become your fan.

Question: How does my ex-girlfriend feel? I didn't beg, plea, or chase after she left me for another guy.
Answer: All the following assumes you haven’t been abusive towards her or anything like that before the breakup. You need to first understand why she left you for another guy in the first place. (sidenote: please use your own discernment to determine which of the following applies best to your situation). If she left you for another man, then she most likely did so because: She feels this other man is superior to you in every way and a better deal for herself This happens because women tend to be opportunists and only date across and up but rarely or never down. Nothing wrong with that per se. We‘re not supposed to sell ourselves short after all. If this applies, she never really wanted you to begin with, only saw you as a temporary distraction from her ex or lost feelings and interest throughout your relationship. In which case the problem was that you overlooked her red flags or that you and her just don’t have the deeper alignment that’s necessary for relationships to last and be of substance in the long-term. She‘s very likely to be the type of woman who waits at the finish line The kind of woman who lacks the patience to help support a man during the build while he’s either just starting out from the bottom or only halfway there. The kind of woman who explicitly goes for men who already achieved the results and fruits of their hard labor (crossed the finish line) which took many years, if not decades to build. Those results and fruits may be high social status, massive dating success, financial wealth, professional success, being very physically fit, very attractive, evolved masculinity, fame, respect, etc. Those are things most of us men need to earn and work for and which don’t just fall into our lap. Such women know this and only go for these men because, again, they don’t really want to help a man to get there. They want a piece of the cake because she has achieved the same level of growth, healing and success or feels that she deserves this, which isn’t always true because women too have an ego and aren’t always assessing their desirableness in dating accurately (there are also men like this out there). So, if #1 or #2 or both apply to you, then she doesn’t love you or lost that love at some point, even if you didn’t chase, beg or plead and went straight no contact post-breakup. Because women who want and love (and therefore respect) their man will not leave him for another man because she believes in you, in your goals and in your vision of a better future. She will stand by your side and support you during the build and wont leave you hanging when you experience setbacks and adversities (which are an inevitable part of life in general. Nobody is immune to setbacks and adversities). She will be a woman who makes you a better, not bitter man. That‘s clearly not your ex-girlfriend. And because of this, you got to wish her well and gracefully move on from her. Focus instead on attracting and keeping the woman who reciprocates, who loves and supports you during the build.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: Can I make it work with an ex again?
Answer: Due to bad social conditioning, there‘s something that many people get wrong about this whole get your ex back thing. And that is that you can’t negotiate romantic interest, reciprocation and attraction. Especially not through begging, overpursuing and pleading. Also not if: You can’t have a relationship with someone like that. If you continue to beg and overpursue, then at best your ex will take you back out of pity, not out of love and respect for you or because they want to be with you, and this won’t last long either. They will dump you again a few days or weeks later. Therefore, and if your own well-being is of any significance to you, you got to stop tolerating a dynamic of unrequited love and stop buying into this false belief that you must 'fight for your ex'. If you really want them back, then you have to learn to be happy and content without them. You will have to display attractive qualities and behaviors. Chasing, overpursuing, refusing to move on and begging aren’t attractive qualities. They make you look weak in your exes eyes and only makes them feel like leaving was the right decision for them. Therefore, walk away, towards something better and stop trying to make it work with someone who is fixated on never being with you again. Focus on becoming and being your best, most attractive, most healed and most powerful self. Realize that chasing an ex is a shit strategy that never works.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: Does no contact really work? I’m confused what to do to get her back.
Answer: This depends on what your intention with no contact is. If it‘s only to get her back, you‘re doing it from the from place, namely from a place of fear and unhealthy co-dependency. Your ex-girlfriend knows and intuitively senses this too. And it‘s because of this that she will most likely never come back, even if you go completely silent on her. Because it‘s manipulative and insecure and also obvious. Therefore, realize and accept that no contact isn’t a magic pill or a manipulative tactic to get an ex back (as is often wrongfully assumed). It’s first and foremost supposed to help you reconnect with yourself, not with your ex. It‘s a very mature, highly effective and wise lifestyle choice you make and a boundary you set when: So again, never use no contact with the intention to get your ex back, otherwise it will not work and backfire on you very fast. Instead, do it to reconnect with yourself. To improve yourself, to rediscover life without them, to put your own well-being first, to put an end to being a simp, to walk away from situations of unrequited love and to respect yourself. Anything else is insanity and doesn’t work. If you still don’t believe me, then consider that if it’s been more than a few months post-breakup and you have been in contact sporadically, you would have long reconciled already if she still wanted you and if the relationship were of substance. Therefore, you really don’t have any other option besides going no contact, walking away and massively improving yourself. It‘s the only thing that will improve things for you.

Question: How long should you wait to date after getting over an ex?

They have to respect this and deal with the fact that you do not accept their behaviors or offers for friendship anymore. They have to accept that they can no longer have their cake and eat it too. Important sidenote: if you have kids together, choose low contact over full no contact. This means keeping interactions with your ex at an absolute minimum, to only reach out to or respond to them to handle the kids stuff. If possible, try to create a set schedule with your ex for the days where you get the kids and the days where they they get them. Also, don’t use your kids as an excuse to gain access to your ex. Don’t constantly ask them if they have time to talk or something like that. Keep your interactions as minimal as possible and only reach out when it’s something important that has to do with the kids. Because your ex is going to feel the shift in your energy and personality either way as long as you work on yourself. Improve your mindset You can’t always control your thoughts but you can be aware of the nature and direction of them and change it from there. I.e. when you catch yourself slipping back into endless rumination, put your foot down and decide to no longer go down this path, because so far it has only made things worse for yourself. Therefore, intentionally put your focus elsewhere, to something that helps you heal or get ahead in life. Because to a large degree, the quality of our mindset dictates the quality of our life, well-being, success and personal growth. Make sure that your mind is working for you, not against you. Follow the 1% rule The 1% rule is a simple yet very powerful habit that helps you focus on growth, to improve yourself and rebuild self-confidence. All you need to do is to reflect on your day before going to bed and ask yourself: ‘Am I smarter/more aware/better than yesterday?’ If for you the answer is that you only got 1% better/more aware/smarter than yesterday, then that’s still a win and it means that you have won, that you have done the right thing and are on the right track. Do this every single day before going to bed and you’ll be 365% better by the next year.

Question: Why is ghosting so hurtful?

It ended very abruptly and unexpectedly and you‘re left wondering what the f just happened and wanting more. Works the same way with being ghosted or with not having gotten closure. Here’s how to properly heal from and bounce back from this: Closure isn’t as relevant to the healing process as you think it is We really don’t need it from our exes/ex ghosters in order to finally move on, properly heal and be self-confident again. Sure, getting this open, honest and clear conversation from your ex surely makes things easier. However, you can move on and heal without it (I explain how in the next points). It just adds more obstacles to the entire healing process. Those are obstacles that everyone can overcome Not saying it‘s easy. I‘m pointing out that even if you got ghosted in the most painful way with no closure whatsoever, there is a path through and out of this. Also that healing from breakups isn’t a thing that happens with the snap of a finger. Rather, it‘s a gradual and non-linear process of emotionally building yourself up, self-discovery, letting go, personal growth and building self-awareness and self-confidence. Closure speeds this process up a bit but, it never does the whole job. Focus on the facts You may not know all the details and the specifics behind your exes decisions and behaviors, and you may not fully understand what went wrong or what you did that contributed to this. But neither do you really need to figure that out. All that you really need to know to get a sense of finality right now is this: Remember that these facts and results are more relevant than the specifics that you can only speculate about. Be firm with your boundaries with them Many ghosters eventually come back around. But when they do, it‘s important that you either remain consistent with no contact or don’t immediately take them back and don’t jump into a reconciliation. Because they may not have changed at all and only come back for self-centered reasons. Once they’ve gotten what they wanted from you, they are very likely to ghost again at some point. Therefore, don’t get involved with highly inconsistent people who only add pain to your life. Choose men or women who choose you and who have a spine. Let the rest go.

Question: Men who think it’s okay to be vulnerable with women are at risk of having a failed relationship? Isn’t this true?
Answer: It’s very true but, not for the reasons you think. It’s true because a lot of modern men don’t understand what real vulnerability is and because there is a shortage of modern women out there who aren’t as empathetic, emotionally mature and emotionally intelligent as is often assumed. For this reason, I will explain what real vulnerability looks like. To understand this, you need to first be aware of the difference between authentic vulnerability and emotional dumping, because a lot of men often confuse these two but, they’re not the same thing. Emotional Dumping It’s when someone unloads their emotions onto someone else without consideration for the other persons capacity or willingness to receive that information. It often involves overwhelming the listener with an unfiltered outpouring of feelings and problems. This is what that would look like: Uncontrolled and Unfiltered: Lack of self-control and filtering, leading to an overwhelming outpour of emotions. One-Sided: It tends to be one-sided, with the one doing the emotional dumping focusing solely on their own needs without regard for the listeners feelings or boundaries. Inappropriate Timing: Emotional dumping often occurs without considering the timing or setting, leading to inappropriate or inconvenient situations for the listener (i.e. pouring your feelings out to your girlfriend while you’re out together in public or with friends isn’t the right moment to do that). Seeking short-term relief: The primary aim is often personal relief, rather than seeking understanding or support. So, this is why a woman would dump her man after he dumped her feelings and problems onto her — it’s because he’s been overly needy and selfish and made her feel like she constantly has to mother him. No woman really wants that because it’s annoying and makes her feel used or manipulated. Authentic vulnerability It involves sharing your innermost thoughts, feelings, and experiences in a way that preserves your self-respect or dignity and opens you up to the possibility of emotional harm but also allows for deeper connection and intimacy. It requires honesty, trust, and the courage to be open about your true self. This is what that would look like: Intentional and Thoughtful: Vulnerable sharing is intentional and often involves a degree of thoughtfulness about what to share and with whom. Reciprocal: Healthy vulnerability often involves a give-and-give where both parties share and listen. Context-Appropriate: The timing and setting are considered; the sharer is mindful of the other persons emotional state and context. Seeking Understanding and Support: The aim is to seek understanding, connection, and support rather than simply offloading emotions. Solution oriented & personal responsibility: The sharer doesn’t forget that what they are revealing is their own responsibility (I.e. they don’t expect their girlfriend to solve their emotional problems for them because they already have a solution). And therein lies the problem — a lot of men seek understanding, support and connection with a woman who lacks empathy, who has a low level of emotional intelligence. Who doesn’t support them, doesn’t want to understand them, with whom they don’t yet have established a deeper connection. Likewise, they may dump all their emotions and pain onto a girlfriend with whom they do have a deeper connection but end up pushing her away because they don’t understand the above mentioned nuances and differences.

Question: What causes the feeling that everything is meaningless after a breakup?
Answer: Having your dreams, goals and hopes crushed after a breakup sucks and hurts deeply. After all, you've been with them for a long time and thought you found your soulmate, 'the one'. On top of that, it makes you feel powerless. Completely purposeless, hopeless and directionless making you drift through life like a leaf in the wind. But there's a blindspot you're overlooking (no, it has nothing to do with getting them back, with tinder or getting into another relationship as quickly as possible). The blindspot is that you've been putting all eggs in one basket. Because when you concentrate and focus all your efforts and resources (emotional, physical and psychological ones) into just one area of your life (in your case 1 person and 1 relationship), you neglect other important areas of life. So it's only natural for your life to fall apart after a breakup when you do this. But this is never a good foundation. Because buying into the false belief that someone else can complete you is an overly romanticized approach to relationship that sucks. Because building success and living a life with purpose, stability and substance is about investing your energy and resources wisely. It's about having a balance and diversity. A balance between taking care of and focusing on relationships, your overall health, your personal /spiritual growth, your career/finances/business and your passions. Without such a balance, your life is built on fragile foundations and all it takes for it to fall apart is just one temporary setback like rejection or a breakup. So, the lessons this pain teaches you are these: Build a stronger foundation When you feel hopeless and lost or purposeless for a long time after the breakup, this is a sign you're facing the consequences of neglecting other important aspects of your life and that you have put all eggs in one basket in the past relationship. Because when you rely and depend too heavily on one single relationship or person to feel worthy, to get meaning, purpose or direction from them and to make you happy/self-confident/content/whatever, you’re not just putting unnecessary pressure on them and the relationship to be perfect (a standard that’s not humanly possible to be fulfilled consistently), you’re also making others view you in a less favorable light and push them away. You’ll be giving away your autonomy, independence, self-respect and power and as a byproduct of that feel destroyed, worthless and lost when that person or thing you depend on too much leaves and exits your life. Create a purpose that goes beyond one single person, beyond dating and relationships You can (and are supposed to) create a deeper purpose that goes beyond dating and relationships so that even when a relationship ends you still have an amazing life to look forward to and never really feel lost without the ex. Because again, your life is built on too fragile foundations if you rely and depend too heavily on one single person or thing. Invest in yourself So that you can become a healed person who solved most of their problems, so that you can create the success you want and so that you become someone who not only attracts the right people but also builds and sustains healthy, stable and amazing relationships with them. Learn to embrace the power of diversity in all aspects of your life Meaning that rather than letting other peoples behaviors or decisions and fleeting external circumstances control and dictate the way you feel, and rather than constantly chasing validation, you start to derive core-confidence from your own competence, self-respect and self-realization. From the deep and inner knowing that you find a way through adversity no matter what, that there is a way through this and that you walk this way.

Question: Why would an ex want to stay in touch after a breakup? Is there a chance of getting back together or should I move on?

I.e. they don’t fully see how they’re making the healing process harder for the dumpee and how they give false hopes by staying around and giving the impression they still have interest when they truly don’t. To let you down easy Exes pretty much always do this with a good intent but, this approach does more harm than good and backfires because the pain of breakups can be prolonged but not be avoided. That’s why it’s wise to rather than beating around the bush and unneccsarily dragging the breakup out, to cut right through the bullshit, live in truth and end it quickly rather than slowly. This is initially more painful for both but, gives both a more solid foundation upon which they can start to heal, process, grow and let go post-breakup. To keep you around as a back-up plan You know, as their side-chick/side-guy which they only go to when their rebound-relationships go south or when they feel lonely. Such dynamics are always one-sided and truly not worth the long-term pain. They’ll be like an energy vampire in your life who corrodes your self-confidence if you allow them to use you as their side-guy/side-chick because you’ll consistently find yourself feeling used, taken for granted and worthless. To keep you hooked on them In my book, when it comes to breakups and to being the dumper, it’s wise to quickly set clear boundaries, to never keep things open-ended or unclear even if it hurts so that both end things on a peaceful note. That’s not always possible but, worth aiming for. Unfortunately, some exes will intentionally refuse to give closure and keep things open-ended and unclear so that they can keep you guessing and thus have you chase them forever so that you don’t let them go, don’t heal and don’t move on. Because sometimes, they need that reassurance that you need them more than they need you in order to be and feel self-confident. They need to feel like you’re always available for them, otherwise they would lose their self-confidence. The reason they do this is because they’re either high on narcsissism or fear that they can’t process the breakup in case the dumpee moves on for good, which isn’t true because I strongly believe that everyone has the innate and natural ability to heal and bounce back even from the toughest breakups.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: Is it advisable to let an ex who cheated on you back into your life? How can you determine if their intentions are genuine?
Answer: Even if their intentions to change in a positive direction are genuine, it’s not a good idea to take them back after you found out or once they told you. Because eventually, you will resent yourself for having forgiven and taken them back too easily. It will slowly eat you up inside and it may even spoil the entire relationship for you because the trust on your part has been broken. Additionally, your cheating boyfriend/girlfriend may lose even more respect for you because of that. It may make them feel like they can get away with it again because you taking them back too easily gave them the impression that there won’t be any consequences on your part if they cheat. So no. Don’t take them back. Have more self-respect and move on. This will suck for the cheater if they really want to change in a positive direction but, if they truly cared about and loved you they wouldn’t have done that in the first place. They would have either broken up first or made efforts to improve and solve the problems in the relationship.

When both of you have learned and grown from the mistakes you did and when both of you desire a reconciliation at least equally as much. I.e. the interest for a reconciliation has to be mutual and reciprocated. Name: Daniel Subke
Question: What are some ways to move on from an ex who broke up with you, ghosted you, and was not a good friend or partner?
Answer: Build the self-respect and emotional/mental stability to accept that it’s over and to not give your energy, love, commitment and attention away to a girl who repeatedly shows you that she’s for the streets and doesn’t want, love nor respect you. Like, seriously man. Have some dignity. What else needs to happen before you finally put your own well-being first? Do you seriously need her to ignore, ghost, cheat on and hurt you even more? Come on man. Now before you say 'But moving on is so hard…'. Stop being such a whiny simp. Learn to manage your emotions in a productive and self-empowering way. Crying after her way beyond the point where you’ve cried enough isn’t productive nor self-empowering. Because you know what’s even harder and what’s going to cause you even more pain than moving on and letting her go? Holding on to her and telling yourself that she was 'the one' even though she is not worth one tear and even though she has given you a lot of empirical evidence that she’s clearly not worthy of your attention, commitment and energy. She and many other women too will never respect you if you keep doing that shit. They will continue to cheat on and walk all over you if you don’t change in that regard. Your dating life will continue to suck if this doesn’t improve and you will keep attracting more cheaters. So, here’s how to respect yourself again: Set up no contact Then, never reach out to her again. Direct all the energy you would otherwise use to ruminate and cry or chase after her towards yourself and towards the intention to become a more attractive, more self-aware, more powerful and better man. Remind yourself that she has consistently proven to be a girl who adds to your pain and doesn’t contribute anything of value to your life. Your feelings will tell you otherwise but, that’s why you got to let these feelings go and release them. Rediscover your core-confidence True self-confidence comes from within and isn’t dependent on anything outside of you such as your looks, the amount of women you have sex with, situational achievements or fleeting external circumstances. Therefore, learn to emotionally and mentally build yourself up. Take action to create a better life for yourself. Celebrate your wins no matter how big or small. As a modern man, your most valuable asset in the context of dating and relationships is your attention and commitment It becomes obsolete and worthless to women if you give it away to those who don’t love nor want you. If you give it away without her having to earn and reciprocate it. That’s why your ex-girlfriend ignores you despite your best efforts. She lost attraction and just doesn’t value or respect what you have to offer because due to overextending yourself by chasing after her and begging her to come back, she started viewing you as a man with no self-respect. As a man she can cheat on, lie to, manipulate and walk all over without any consequences. This causes her to look down on you, to lose respect. And we can’t love who we don’t respect, because mutual respect is the soil upon which love grows. Therefore, start respecting yourself again. Stop tolerating dynamics of unrequited love. Stop pursuing relationships and reconciliations with emotionally unavailable ex-girlfriends. Instead, direct all your attention towards yourself. Commit to build yourself into a better man, to your goals and to your personal growth.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: Why is it bad to move on straight after a breakup?
Answer: Moving on quickly after a breakup is a double-edged sword. On one hand, immediately jumping into a rebound or not giving oneself enough space to process merely suppresses the pain that needs real processing, self-awareness, introspection and deep letting go work. It’s also that if someone isn’t phased at all by a breakup, they were either never in a real relationship or never truly opened themselves up. On the other hand, not everyone who moves on quickly never truly loved the ex nor cared about them. Sometimes, it’s that they have learned their lessons and have grown enough to cut right through the bullshit and do what works for them in terms of letting go, emotional healing and moving on. I.e. they move on quickly because they have a good relationship with themselves, a solid breakup-plan in place and know what they need to do in order to heal and bounce back quickly. They have learned that while the pain of breakups never truly decreases in intensity, with experience, wisdom and growth we get better at letting go and navigating through it faster.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: Why is my ex not happy that I moved on even though she's the one who broke up with me?
Answer: It‘s either because they expected you to chase, to fight and compete for them or because they’re mad because they can no longer string you along and use you for attention, validation, whatever. This happens because some people will break up to test how authentic and genuine their boyfriends/girlfriends love for them is. They want to test if you will walk away or chase after them. I.e. they think to themselves: 'if they really love me as much as they say they do, then they will chase, fight and compete to be with me again no matter what'. In other words, they want you to beg them to take you back, to degrade yourself and be all miserable without them. They want you to do all the work while they’re doing what they want and don’t give a shit about you. It‘s not a smart thing to do, pretty immature and also a red flag. Because while this is a romantic ide...

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: How come during a breakup my ex seems to be doing great while I'm not?
Answer: It’s always because of one or more of these reasons: They were never as invested in the relationship as you‘ve been I.e. whatever you had going on wasn’t a balanced dynamic of an equal give and give but a dynamic where you‘ve been giving 80% and they were giving you 20%. It‘s what happens when we lose ourselves in a relationship with someone who makes us feel like we need to earn and fight really hard or compete for their love and attention. With someone who never really loved you much and who has been giving you the will but not the heart. You were their rebound and their intention was never to build a stable, healthy and amazing union with you Their intention was to use you as a temporary distraction from their pain of the previous breakup or as a pawn they can use to make their ex jealous so they come back around. As some kind of warm-up to build their confidence for the men or women they really want. Once they felt that you helped them heal, build and distract themselves enough, or once they got their ex back, you stopped being of any use to them and thus they dumped you. You wanted the relationship of a lifetime, they wanted a temporary distraction. They have more experience and wisdom than you when it comes to overcoming breakups I.e. they have already learned what works and doesn’t work for them in terms of emotional healing and letting go of an ex. Therefore, they cut right through the bullshit and take the steps that work for them in order to heal and to create the results they want. To them, the relationship felt like a prison Now that it’s over, they feel liberated and as if they can be themselves again. And if the relationship was like that for them, chances are it was like that for you too, you just haven’t been as aware of it due to rose-colored glasses. They were prepared and emotionally/psychologically checked out while still being with you Many times, the warning signs of this are there. It’s just that when there’s an awareness-gap between both, the dumpee recognizes this too late or the dumper was never opening up about how they felt because deep down they didn’t want to heal and improve whatever was wrong in the relationship. Because of that, you and them are on polar opposites of the healing process. How to overcome this: Decide which path you want to go Do you want to continue keeping tabs on your ex for the following months, if not years and then complain about how unfair it is that they have already moved on and healed (which keeps the ex alive in your mind)? Or do you want to heal, to love and respect yourself and feel and be self-confident again? To stand in your power (which makes you prioritize your own well-being)? You can’t have both. Therefore, make a decision on which path you want to walk. If it’s the latter, then you got to be consistent and stick with that decision no matter what. You’ll have to hold yourself accountable. To stop keeping tabs on them, go no contact, let go, make intentional efforts to rebuild self-love/self-respect, rediscover life without them and get back on track. Some exes are good at putting on a front of success and well-being Outwardly, they may appear as if they don’t give a shit about you to make you think they don’t care but in reality, they still carry the pain with them. They just don’t show it because they don’t want you to feel like they still care. It’s not a good way to approach it because it obviously doesn’t create the deeper healing people need. Therefore, stop comparison game. The only person worth comparing yourself to is your past self to measure and assess your progress and your growth.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: Why is my ex-girlfriend of 2 years that I broke up with 2 months ago doing better than me?
Answer: How come you‘re still comparing yourself to and keeping tabs on her? How come you’re making your self-confidence and worth dependent on an ex-girlfriends feelings for you and not on your competence, your power and your ability to heal and grow? Don’t you see how you’re keeping yourself stuck by doing that? Don’t you have your own goals and a life ahead of you that you need to focus on and take care of? Have you forgotten that you owe yourself a break from all the chasing and pursuing that’s never going anywhere and only hurting you? Have you forgotten that the only person worth comparing yourself to is your past self to measure and assess how far you‘ve come and what still needs to be done?

Question: Why do women always break up and terminate a relationship and right away start meeting or dating without any regret?
Answer: Because a lot of modern women breakup emotionally, spiritually and psychologically while they’re still in the relationship and long or shortly before physically leaving. During this process of disconnecting on an energetic and subconscious level, they often start dating again to secure their rebound-option which they have better chemistry with and who they think is a better man in many aspects. Because a lot of modern women have an opportunistic mindset which causes them to date across and up but never down. Once they have secured their rebound, they dump their man, move on and remain fixated on never coming back, especially if she feels that she’s 'upgrading' her ex and thinks that she has given him many chances to improve whatever she wanted him to improve. And many times they’ve been correct with thinking this way. However, sometimes they were wrong about it and due to unhealthy amounts of pride simply overestimated how quickly they can get over an ex and heal from a breakup and underestimated the effort and work this really takes. Because especially if she’s a non-committal woman with poor emotional and mental health, she will believe in the saying of 'the best way to get over someone is to get under another one', which in my book is a surface-level and superficial solution which doesn’t address nor heal the root-cause. In this case, and especially if she still has many unrpcoessed feelings for him or sees her ex doing really well and improving without her, she will eventually come back around. But at this point, it‘s often too late because men who genuinely worked on themselves after the breakup and during no contact will have let her go, healed and moved on.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: How do I win an argument with someone who is both ignorant and certain?
Answer: You can’t. Because the thing about ignorant people who refuse to think outside the box is that they are unwilling to grow, to open their minds to different perspectives and different possibilities. This happens a lot when dumpees chase after their ex and try to convince them to come back. The dumper usually doesn’t want the relationship anymore and doesn’t care about seeing the dumpees side because they’ve made up their mind and are fixated on never going back again. The result of this is that the dumpee feels like talking against a wall and only becomes more frustrated the harder they try because the dumper won’t change their mind. That’s one reason why chasing after a dumper ex is a shit strategy that never works and why the wise thing to do here is to accept that they cannot change nor control the way the dumper feels about the dumpee.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: What break up mistakes that makes you suffer more?
Answer: One very common one is waiting for and expecting a new person to make up for the wrongdoings of an ex. I.e. carrying all the unprocessed emotional baggage (hurt and resentment towards the ex) from the previous relationship into a new one. The reason this makes us suffer longer and more is that nobody wants to nor likes being held responsible for things they haven’t done and because it often does make new relationships worse when in reality they have a pretty good foundation. So, whether your ex cheated on you, hurt you deeply, let you down countless times, made you lose faith in humanity, took you for granted, whatever, it’s not other peoples job to make up for it. This is why forgiveness is an important part of the healing process. If we don’t heal our wounds, don’t forgive and keep holding on to the resentment, we will eventually let it out and project it onto others who didn’t deserve it and who do have good intentions for as well as love us. However, to forgive doesn‘t mean to forget or that we take the person who hurt us back, that their wrongdoings suddenly become okay. It obviously wasn’t okay and it was unfair and they are a piece of shit for having done whatever they did. All it means is to prioritize our own inner peace over the poison of resentment and choose to heal whatever needs healing. To release the hold the past wrongdoings of an ex has over us. This is the best revenge. It‘s doing well, being successful and showing them that their attempts to destroy you were futile.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: How painful are breakups?
Answer: Very often, they’re among the most painful and darkest experience one can have in life. It’s this kind of pain that you wouldn’t wish on your worst enemy. And the thing about it is that the intensity and depth of the pain is proportional to the depth and intensity of love you experienced in that relationship. I.e. the deeper the hurt, the more it shows how much you truly cared about and loved your person. How much the relationship meant to you. If people aren’t so hurt by a breakup at all, it shows that what they had wasn’t a real relationship or that they never truly opened themselves up to true intimacy. Also, as long as work with the pain, it facilitates a lot of healing, personal growth and transformations. That’s not to say it’s an easy process. It’s just that eventually and somehow, you’ll always come out on the good end and as a new version of yourself. Because it’s a process of maturing, building resilience and of overcoming adversity. The lessons, wisdom and growth you gain and exerience during that process will stick with you forever. It will be a thing that gives you a sense of deep core-confidence and self-reliance.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: My ex moved on so fast. How can I overcome the pain?
Answer: Simply put, because they have been prepared and you weren't. On their side, there has been a process of emotionally and mentally checking out while you were still together and while you were under the impression that everything is cool. I.e. you thought that you had the perfect deal whereas they had already made up their mind and just weren't as emotionally invested in it as you were. This happened long or shortly before they physically left. And during this process, they either started seeing someone new who they planned to secure as their rebound option or were busy creating their post-breakup plan. This is why you can't expect them to feel anything close to what you're feeling right now, because you and them are on a completely different stage in the healing process. You both are on polar opposites of the scale. This is why comparing yourself to them in terms of the healing process isn't going to help you in any way, shape or form. So, don't try to compete with them. Instead, focus on taking care of, solving and healing what you are experiencing right now. What they do doesn't matter and it's completely irrelevant to your healing process, though it’s valid to hate and judge them harshly for leaving the way they did.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: Why do people who dump their ex come back to their ex some time later?
Answer: Because they made the decision to breakup without clearly thinking it through first. I‘m saying this because I never really regretted the decision to break up with the girlfriends that I broke up with. Nor did I ever go back. But this was only so because I properly thought it through first and had a post-breakup plan in place. Unfortunately, some dumpers don’t have a post-breakup plan because they overestimate how quickly they can heal from a breakup and let go of an ex and underestimate the effort this really takes. Therefore, they only realize that their decision was rushed when their dumpee started to accept the breakup, to heal, rediscovers life without them and genuinely lets go on an emotional and psychological level during no contact. Because that’s the point where the type of dumper I described above experiences the full consequences of their decision to leave first. Where they get to experience what life is like without the relationship. Now this doesn’t mean that the dumpers decision to break up was wrong. It may very well have been the right thing for both but, it just means that the dumper has bit off more than they could chew because again, they underestimated the effort and work it takes to get over an ex. Because of that, they come back around hoping that they can get a piece of the improved version of the dumpee.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: Does time really heal the pain?
Answer: No. Time heals physical wounds but this alone doesn’t heal emotional and psychological wounds. This is especially true in the context of breakups. People don’t heal and get over their ex because they waited forever to feel better. They created this result because they realized that relying solely on time to heal us only numbs the pain and makes our problems compound. Because the longer we wait and sit idly by, the more momentum we give our unwanted thought/feeling/and behavioral patterns to become more and more natural. So natural that we reach a point where we’re not even aware of them being there. And this creates massive problems in our life. Therefore, relying solely on time isn’t good. The formula for real emotional healing post-breakup looks like this: Awareness + Patience + Letting go/Radical acceptance + Intentional efforts to create positive change inside out + Massive action. So, what we need isn’t just time. It’s self-compassion, growth and positive forward momentum on a psychological and emotional level. It’s making an effort to become a more aware and more conscious being, to improve the relationship with oneself.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: Do dumpers ever feel as hurt as the dumpee or not at all?
Answer: I’ll give you the raw truth about this. What a lot of dumpees don’t realize about it, and some of y’all will hate me for pointing this out, is that dumpers aren’t always these horrible, narcissistic human beings with no soul. Quiet frequently, the dumper has been hurting during the relationship just as much as you the dumpee hurts right now post-breakup. In fact, it’s not uncommon that they’ve been trying and trying to communicate their feelings, to get you to understand them. They’ve been waiting and waiting for you to improve whatever behavior or attitude on your part contributed to the breakup and gradually made them feel more and more unloved, unseen and unheard. Now why did they wait? Well, because they loved you enough to be patient and to understand where you’re coming from. And when this goes on for too long, dumpers get tired of this bullshit. They get tired of feeling like they’re talking against a wall, of feeling as if they’re the ones who carry the entire relationship only for it to be an extremely draining, painful, unrewarding and unfulfilling experience. Because of this, they eventually reach a breaking point where they simply have enough, put their foot down and just don’t give a shit about you anymore — because they’ve already done this for long enough without it having been reciprocated the right way. In a way that made them feel loved. Because we all owe ourselves the right to feel loved the right way. If we fail to do this, we push our girlfriends/boyfriends away. We will give them the subliminal message that we don’t want, love nor respect them when in fact we do. And therein lies the thing that will help every dumpee heal faster and get over their ex — it’s to own your chunk that contributed to it. It’s to see the ways in which you have co-created this breakup. Because that’s the only thing we can change/improve and have a lot of power and control over.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: What are the effects of breaking up and getting back together repeatedly, and how can one recognize the signs of a toxic relationship?
Answer: The most destructive effect of on-off dynamics that both of you will inevitably experience is relationship burnout. You will know when this happens. Because your body and entire system will tell you that you must stop going back and forth with this person. Your ex will experience the same. And the longer we ignore these signals, the worse and more painful they become. This is how your body will tell you that it’s a toxic relationship, that the person you’re with just isn’t it and that you experience relationship burnout:

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: Why do people often hope that the person who initiates a breakup (the dumper) will regret their decision, even if the breakup was for valid and positive reasons?
Answer: Simply put, because they don’t want to accept that it’s over and want to feel like they’re in control and the more powerful one in the dynamic between them and their dumper. I.e. they want to be in this position where the tables have turned, where they are now the pursued one and where they need their ex less than the ex needs them. And it does feel amazing to have a dumper ex blow up your phone and beg for you to come back after all the work you‘ve put in. But honestly, this is a shit approach that sucks. Which is why you will never really see me promoting this kind of mindset. This approach doesn’t heal the core-wound, turns breakups into a competition, keeps the ex alive in your mind, makes you too outcome dependent and merely provides a temporary ego-boost but more often than not doesn’t solve/improve the underlying problems and behaviors that contributed to the breakup, perpetuating unhealthy on-off cycles with an ex. It can serve as motivational fuel to help people get the ball rolling and take action but, there are better and also easier ways to create the same result. One is to realize that more often than not, your ex did you a huge favor by dumping you and by ending the relationship before you wanted it to end. In fact, it‘s not uncommon for people to be insanely glad they never chased after nor gotten back with their ex because through healing properly, they started to see all the major problems in their past relationship that they haven’t been aware of before or deliberately chose to ignore. Besides, true power is being able to bounce back after a horrific breakup and successfully having overcome and mastered the challenges of no contact.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: Is it possible for an ex to still have feelings for their former partner even after moving on with someone else?
Answer: Based on my observations after having coached a fair number of people through breakups for several years, it‘s common for people to still have relatively strong feelings for their ex despite already being in a relationship. This is just a pattern that I see consistently and over and over again. And from what I‘ve learned, the reason it is that way is because: Because of that, a lot of people carry their unspoken and unexpressed feelings for their ex around for a really long time, unaware of that this very thing makes their future relationships worse because that emotional baggage (which consists of pain, deep insecurities, fears, projections) does affect it. The only people with genuine and authentic indifference towards their ex are those who healed and processed their breakup properly. Meaning that they didn’t immediately jump into a rebound relationship but took a break from dating for a couple of months and used that time to introspect, invest in themselves and heal to the point where they’re no longer run by the breakup and rediscovered their core-confidence.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: How do you move on when you don't want to? How can you stop being in love with somebody, even when they have moved on?
Answer: Well, if you don’t want to move on and prefer to continue to suffer, then that’s what you will get more of — stagnation and more suffering. Because the way this works is that we can’t have the comfort of familiarity, of what feels safe and known and the results of emotional healing, personal growth and positive change. We can’t have both. Therefore, pick your poison. Do you want to keep holding on to the past and do absolutely nothing to break through your unwanted patterns? Fine, then do that. To each their own. However, if you want to move on, then you have to make a conscious decision to do that and also stick with it in the long run through self-accountability. No more going back. Ever. Make an agreement with yourself to never go back again, to do whatever you can to make life better for yourself and to grow into the kind of person you want to be.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: I can’t stay friends with my ex, does that make me an immature person?
Answer: No. It makes you someone with self-respect who doesn’t tolerate a dynamic of self-destruction and unrequited love and who wont allow themselves to be used for sex by an emotionally unavailable ex who doesn’t want them. Don’t listen to people who tell you that it’s immature to not be friends with an ex. It’s usually only said by people who love to string themselves and their ex along for years. Talking about meaningless friends with benefits situationships that never really go anywhere beyond the sex and physical attraction.

Name: Daniel Subke
Question: My ex wants to be friends with me. Is it right? What do I do?
Answer: Assuming you’re the dumpee, this is what you need to know and how to best navigate through this. Don’t agree to their offer for friendship if you still want more Reason I’m saying this and why this is so important to follow is because when people agree to stay friends with their ex even though they still want more and hope for it to turn into a reconciliation at some point, they’re setting themselves up for even more pain. Because more often than not, dumper exes offer friendship to soften the blow for themselves, not because they still have any authentic interest in their ex and dumpees agree to such offers because they think and hope they can ‘work it out’ eventually, because they haven’t properly healed from and emotionally processed the breakup yet, causing them to come from a place of fear and desperation. And when we’re driven by fear, we don’t make good decisions. So, both of these motivations are inherently self-centered and got nothing to do with love. Knowing this, you need to understand that this is a very bad foundation which makes it nearly impossible to ever have an improved relationship with them again that’s even better than the first try. Question their intentions Unfortunately, we’re not living in a perfect world where everyone wants the best for each other. Occasionally, there will be people in our lives who for whatever reason don’t have good intentions for us. Question: If a girl chooses another guy over me in a triangle situation but clearly still has romantic feelings for me, should I be her friend if she offers?

That’s why the decision to take them back is up to you. All I can say regarding this is do what you feel is in your own best interest.

Question: What’s the most insightful thing you’ve learned about women?
Answer: All the following is based on my personal reference experience with women and should be taken with a grain of salt. When it comes to getting a girlfriend, intentional action always trumps hesitation and inaction A lot of men (my past self included) miss their shot with or get friendzoned by a girl whose attraction for him is on point not because they don’t make 7 figures a year, don’t have the abs and aren’t 6ft tall. They miss their shot and eventually get blown off by her because they were too stuck in their head, hesitant and passive when they were supposed to act and overpursued when they were supposed to pull back. More often than not, this happens because they don’t match well with this girl (happens all the time), because guys either have a bad understanding of how attraction in general works, don’t know what they want from her or because there’s some sort of emotional/psychological blockage preventing them from just going ahead and asking her out, being intimate with her or making a clear move. This blockage is either a fear of rejection or low self-esteem (thinking and feeling like he isn’t good enough for her). So, men can be 6ft tall, look their best, hit the gym all they want and make several millions a year but if they suck at taking the lead and at acting in the right moments, they will remain single and eventually keep getting rejected by women despite being a ‘good man’. That’s why looks and money don’t matter as much as most men think. Why when it comes to getting a girlfriend, early on in the getting to know each other stage, men need to learn and be clear about: The reason I’m saying all this is because: The skill that’s worth developing to get better at all this is social skills and emotional awareness. Because women tend to be indirect and emotional communicators. They want you to read between the lines and not take everything at face value. Building social skills and emotional awareness helps you to understand her better in that regard and thus act in the right moments. Attraction works like a volume-knob, not a light switch What I mean by this is that attraction isn’t this thing that’s either on or off. In reality, attraction constantly fluctuates and works more like a volume-knob. I.e. depending on your behavior and some other factors, a womans attraction for you may start out at around 80 db on a decibel scale of 0–100, drops to 30 db and may go up to 90 db. This is a good thing. It’s a good thing because it means there’s pretty much always a way to bring the attraction from 0 db back to 80 or even 100. It’s also a good thing because it means that you can bounce back after having been too needy or friendzoned, though it won’t always be easy. And at the end of the day, attraction is what draws a woman to you whereas love, mutual respect and commitment is what keeps you together and her in your life. The more a woman loves, respect, wants and is attracted to you, the more forgiving she will be Whereas the lower all that is, the more unforgiving she becomes. Meaning that if she really loves you, your room for mistakes will be pretty big because she trusts and believes in you a lot. If she doesn’t love you or when her level is too low though, that room for mistakes gets increasingly smaller because the trust and respect isn’t there.

Question: Why does it seem like getting your ex back doesn't work forever?

It‘s telling you: 'Hold up, this isn’t for your highest good. Let me redirect you to a better path'.
