Question: What is the best thing that one realises after a break-up?
Answer: There are a few. Life is a massive grey zone What I mean by this is that relationships don’t end because of one single mistake that one side did. That’s an overly simplified and inaccurate way to think about it. The reality is that breakups happen because of a fundamental lack of alignment. Because of a culmination of many bad decisions, bad behaviors or many small and big mistakes on both sides. This is why people who blame it all on their ex and act as if they have done absolutely nothing that contributed to that usually struggle the most to process a breakup, to emotionally heal from it and to build better relationships afterwards. Why it would take them many years to truly let go of an ex. So again, breakups aren’t the fault of just one side. It’s that both you and your ex contributed to it to different degrees. I.e. through your behaviors, decisions and actions, you may have contributed 30% to it whereas your ex contributed 70% to it. But it’s never ever 100% on one side and 0% on the other. Life and relationships are a lot more nuanced than that. You will learn this yourself once you really start to grow through the experience of the breakup, take ownership of your chunk and improve the behaviors that contributed to it. This is how you drastically speed up the healing process. What your ex thinks of you is completely and utterly meaningless and irrelevant unless you make it a big deal People are severely limiting their own potential and holding themselves back a great deal simply by caring too much of what their ex thinks of them. By placing such high importance on that that they forget to put themselves first. The result of this is that they neglect themselves, remain stuck in their head and don’t really heal, all while their ex has long moved on. That’s why it’s not a big deal if your ex thinks low of you when you decide to go no contact, when you refuse their offer for friendship because you don’t want to tolerate a dynamic of unrequited love and when you block, unfollow and delete them everywhere. If they think you’re being immature for doing that, then so be it. Their perception of you isn’t accurate anyway. It’s 90% based on their own projections, beliefs and mindsets, and you can’t control or change that. Don’t let other people determine who to stay with and who to leave Because there are a lot of dishonest and manipulative people in this world who experience jealousy and simply don‘t want others to have what they feel they lack themselves. Because of that, they will try to sabotage others relationships by spreading lies about your girlfriend/boyfriend to change your perception of that gf/bf in such a negative way that you will want to leave and stay away from them. Likewise, some people around your ex may have told lies about you to make you look very bad so that your ex will dump you and choose the person that lied to them about you. What this ultimately reveals is that when an ex believes the lies someone says about you or when you believe the lies you’re being told about your gf/bf, there’s usually no love or respect involved. It means that your ex is either extremely gullible and naive or never really appreciated you until it was too late and until the truth was revealed (it‘s always revealed, just a matter of time). That when you leave someone solely because of the lies you‘ve been told about them and without first checking if what you‘ve been told is the truth or not, you‘re being easy to manipulate. That’s why it‘s very important to never allow other people to interfere in your relationship. Not even very close family members and friends. Because your relationship is truly none of their business. It‘s only between you and the person you‘re with. Others have no right to sabotage or destroy it. They have no say in it.

Question: What are the signs of a toxic girlfriend?

I.e. rather than directly stating her problem within the relationship or with his behaviors so that she and her man can have a mature and adult discussion about a solution, she will give the silent treatment or emotionally withdraw and be very cold as a way to get him to figure out what’s wrong and essentially let him carry the entire relationship. Controlling A toxic girlfriend will try to control how you spend your money, who you’re looking at, what you wear, things of that nature. Her goal with this is to weaken and emasculate her boyfriend, to make him feel like he’s incompetent and can’t live without her so that he depends more on her and so that she can control and manipulate him even further. She also wont give her man the space and freedom he needs to stand in his power and to be himself, because that would lower her level of control over him. At the root of this behavior are deep trust issues which more often than not aren’t even her boyfriends fault. Emotional abuse The way that a toxic girlfriend emotionally abuses her boyfriend is that she will often gaslight him into believing and thinking that he’s responsible ot make her happy and that her trust issues are his fault. That it’s his job to manage her feelings for her, to make up for the bad behaviors such as cheating or manipulation of her ex-boyfriends. When in reality, he got nothing to do with that and it’s not at all his obligation to heal it for her. It‘s not his fault that in the past, she consistently went for men with a dark triad personality and thus got burned despite knowing better. She’s responsible to take care of these wounds and to heal them herself first and foremost. That’s not to say she can’t ask for help and support. She absolutely can and it’s in her own best interest to do so. A lot of men are even willing to offer their support as long as they love their girlfriend. However, a toxic girlfriend consistently forgets that her trust issues are her problem and that her boyfriend can’t solve it for her or save her from that. That only she herself can do that. Disrespect While the disrespect a boyfriend gets from his girlfriend is sometimes because he isn’t being assertive, powerful or masculine enough and too easily manipulated, very often a toxic girlfriend disrespects and walks all over her boyfriend because she’s immature, emotionally unhealthy and just never learned how to respect a respectable man when she’s being with one. She just doesn’t know how to behave well and how to keep a good man in her life due to the aforementioned immaturity and lack of emotional health. Constant testing Most women are hardwired to test a mans self-confidence and level of self-respect. And it’s even beneficial for relationships if it’s not overdone. However, when the testing reaches a point where she always doubts him despite him embodying true core-confidence and self-respect, she’s being toxic and very unpleasant to be around. It‘s pushing men away because no man wants to chase after their girlfriends approval all the time, especially not if she lacks self-awareness and doesn’t bring much to the table besides beauty and sex.

Question: I found out that I am one of my girlfriend's side guys. What should I do? I love her more than anyone.

She wouldn’t use you for attention and validation and then disappear for a while again. She wouldn’t have such an insatiable craving for and addiction to male attention that she needs to manipulate multiple men into chasing her so thar she feels worthy and good enough. Where a lot of people out there have deep resentment for the opposite gender and will juggle multiple boyfriends/girlfriends, and often times they do so in secret, behind the scenes. They will have a couple of side-guys/side-chicks to cope with their fear of solitude, their self-hatred or with the fact that their 'main-guy/girl' rejected and doesn’t want them. Someone who doesn’t need side-guys/girls in the first place.

Question: Does the dumper really want the dumpee to forget them completely?
Answer: It depends on how deep, meaningful and integral the relationship was for the dumper. If it wasn’t an integral and substantial part of their life, or if it stopped being so midway in the relationship, then they wont care about the dumpee at all and any attempt to change that will usually backfire or just not work. Because they will be fixated on never being with them again. If however the relationship was a substantial and integral part of their life, then they wont want to lose the power and control they have over their dumpee. I.e. they wont want you to fully let go and walk away because they derive most of their self-confidence from the fact and reassurance that you need them more than they need you. That’s why dumpers will give their dumpees breadcrumbs, try to keep them in limbo and fuck with their mind and heart. It‘s also why no contact has to be implemented if the intention is to heal and thrive without the dumper.

Question: Why do people like to ruin other people?

Question: Is it beneficial to seek closure during a breakup or is it better to move on without looking back?
Answer: In the context of breakups, closure is a byproduct of an unprocessed emotional attachment to your ex. It‘s you waiting for them to give you permission to let them go, to accept that whatever you had is over and to start living your life again. Because you still believe that your ex is responsible for how you feel and that they alone have the power to complete, save and heal you. To make all your problems go away. None of this is true of course. It‘s just a belief. A survival mechanism and outdated thought-pattern that you once assigned a certain meaning to that once served to keep you safe and ensure your survival but no longer serves you now because it’s an outdated belief. Right now, you don’t need anyone outside of you to survive. The power to complete, save and heal you is already and has always been in you but never in your ex. That’s why it’s time to give this belief back to whoever gave it to you. To rediscover and maintain your independence, autonomy and emotional fortitude. So, is it beneficial to seek and wait for closure? The answer is that it only benefits and strengthens the emotional attachment to them. That it reinforces this idea and outdated belief I mentioned above. Other than that, you absolutely don’t need closure. What you need is to learn radical acceptance. To radically accept that:

Question: How do I know if I'm over a bad breakup?

Rather, you feel indifferent about it and wish them well. It’s more natural for you to be and feel self-confident, good, enthusiastic about life and enjoy your own presence during solitude than it is to overthink or ruminate and obsess over the breakup situation and your ex. When thinking about them, it gets increasingly easier to focus on something else and not get lost in endless rumination. The intensity and duration of the emotions, feelings and thoughts also decreases. You‘ll become more attractive and start glowing up because you successfully let go of the past, learned from it instead and healed whatever wounds were there. You‘ll lose interest in even thinking about your ex because you‘ve done that so often that it got tiring and that letting go comes naturally to you. You‘ll feel sexually and emotionally attracted to other men/women without feeling guilty or as if you’re cheating on/betraying your ex.

Question: My girlfriend left me for another guy. There was no warning at all. I’m struggling so hard with this. Does anyone have experience on how to cope with this?

Look out for this kind of woman. For the woman who sticks with you during adversity, during the dark times where you experience failures and setbacks (which btw are part of life and inevitable. Whether or not you take her back is up to you. I don’t recommend taking her back and staying with the woman who stayed with you during your lowest points instead.

Question: What are your thoughts on staying friends with your ex if they broke up with you because they weren't feeling it anymore but now want to stay friends so as not to lose contact?
Answer: There are a couple of very important nuances to this, namely: Staying friends is possible but, it won’t be healthy if both aren’t mature enough yet to not be jealous and controlling when one side dates other people Especially not if there is unrequited love involved. You just got to stop lying to yourself regarding this. It’s also pretty disrespectful to a new boyfriend/girlfriend to stay friends with an ex. It may also push potential new partners away because to a lot of people, this is a red flag. As long as you want more than something platonic, you’ll be shooting yourself in the foot by agreeing to stay friends Not just because you’ll have to constantly hide your true feelings. Also because you would most likely end up in a pattern where you give them the boyfriend/girlfriend treatment while they don’t give you jack shit and never reciprocate. She’s just not worth it and she put herself into that category simply by not being the right woman for you. As long as she stays in your life, she will continue to corrode your self-confidence and suck all life out of you.

Question: Is it beneficial to take time apart after a break-up?

Question: I broke up with my boyfriend after being with him for a year. He hasn't even tried to reach out to me. Should I reach out for him?
Answer: What a lot of people today don’t seem to be aware of is that breakups are no game. That you can’t just dump someone you‘ve built a meaningful relationship with and then expect them to chase after you. That while the breakup may not hurt as much for you because you have a rebound relationship or emotionally checked out long or shortly before physically breaking up, it‘s often times incredibly more difficult for the one on the receiving end of a breakup to heal from it, especially if there’s unrequited love involved and especially if they see you starting a rebound so quickly after leaving. It‘s even so painful and difficult that most people need years just to get to a place where they can accept that it’s really over due to the fact that most people never really learn how to properly process a breakup (if you do it right you can get over and heal from a breakup in 1–3 months). Your ex belongs to those people. So it’s not that he hasn’t reached out because he doesn’t care, no longer loves you or anything like that. He most likely still does love you deep down. It‘s just that after the breakup, and through your emotional unavailability as well as your avoidance and disconnection from him, you have been giving him the impression that: Because of that, at some point he began to respect himself and decided to just let you go and walk away. To stop pursuing a reconciliation with you because he was tired of being manipulated and getting rejected over and over and over again. He just didn’t want to have to chase you all the time, because that shit fucking sucks. It‘s a win-lose situation in which only the one who gets chased wins but where the chaser loses it all, including their self-confidence, self-respect and dignity. Additionally, I need to mention that chasing someone isn’t a sign of love and respect but the byproduct of an unhealthy emotional attachment. A dynamic of true love, stability, intimacy and mutual respect can’t be built on such a fragile foundation. That’s why, regardless of whether you’re a man or a woman, you must take the decision to break up more seriously and not approach it like a game. Before breaking up, think about and reflect on what staying in this relationship is costing you, if the opportunity cost of staying in it is worth it or not. Get very clear on if you’re able and willing to work on a solution to the problem(s) that pushed you to the decision to break up. If you find that the opportunity cost of staying in it is much greater than being single, then leave. Once you left, you got to stay away if you still respect your ex to some degree and want them to heal as well as you do.

Question: People make me feel worthless. What should I do?

Question: What is a good text to send a girlfriend who you want back after a breakup?
Answer: You don’t send them text messages. You send them loving kindness and let them go. Not because others force and pressure you into making this decision against your free will but, because through reflection and introspection, you come to the conclusion by yourself that doing so is what’s in your own best interest. That tolerating a dynamic of unrequited love and pursuing a relationship with an ex who most likely already emotionally/mentally checked out and let go of you to a large degree is against your own best interest and only hurts you. Question: How do I stop stalking my ex for good on social media?
Answer: I‘ll explain first why you have this pattern in the first place. It‘s a byproduct of the unprocessed emotional attachment to them and there because subconsciously, you’re trying to fulfill the purpose of this attachment (which is to ensure your survival, to make you feel whole and safe and secure in your own body) by scanning for the tiniest scraps of confirmation that: This is what you want to see on their social media and the only reason you obsess about it all day. Because when your ex feels this way and when you get this confirmation, it feeds or strengthens the attachment to them and thus gives you a sense of relief from the pain of the breakup (which doesn’t last long). It temporarily makes you feel like it’s not quiet over yet and that everything is fine. Unfortunately, a lot of people confuse this sense of relief for emotional healing and end up craving more relief through these confirmations simply because it feels good and gives them emotional leverage from suffering. They end up in this cycle of neediness where their self-confidence and overall well-being is still too dependent on how the ex feels about them. This is really just a coping mechanism. It’s them being completely hooked on their ex and addicted to their validation still. This is how your overall well-being remains at the mercy of how your ex feels about you. But this isn’t how you get over an ex for real. True healing, letting go of an ex and thriving after a breakup looks very differently. Ideally, you want to be able to maintain emotional stability, a sense of genuine inner peace, self-confidence and autonomy completely without your ex and regardless of how they feel about you or what they do and how they behave. Here’s how to do that: Your ex is not an A-List celebrity, so stop approaching them as if they are one You’re approaching them like a celebrity whenever you monitor what they’re doing. Whenever you make their social media activity a higher priority than your own healing and success in life. You stop approaching them this way when you realize that you can break free from the shackles of attachment by: Block, unfollow and delete them everywhere This includes deleting the fake profiles you use to bypass them having blocked you. Because you will never or just very rarely see on there what you hope to see. It‘s just not helping you to heal but adds more obstacles on your path to breakup-mastery. Therefore, purge your social media from them. This way, you eliminate a majority of the distractions, problems and obstacles that prevent you from truly letting go and healing at a deeper level. You weren’t in a relationship with their social media but with the person they are beyond the screen Their social media is just an extension of their personality and lifestyle but nothing more. They will still be an asshole and still the same person even if they post pictures of their rebound relationship, their improved looks, self-improvement content or wise quotes in their stories. Don’t let it deceive you. Make space to process feelings Because it’s still going to hurt, and most likely it’s going to be a very intense and deep kind of pain that can get very dark at times. But during those moments it’s important to allow yourself to grieve the loss you‘ve experienced. It‘s what allows you to gradually adapt to the changes the breakup initiated on an emotional, spiritual and psychological level. It‘s through this pain and adversity that you get to rediscover life without them and experience some real personal growth. You will not be the same person once you come out on the other end. You will be more self-aware, wiser, more aware, stronger, more powerful, more attractive and more self-confident.

Question: When should you start no contact after a break up?

It’s initially extremely painful but, it’s what equalizes the power dynamic and allows both of you to facilitate the healing that’s needed. Because you wont end up in situationships that never lead anywhere and thus speed up the healing process.

Question: What is the healthiest way to get over a breakup?
Answer: These are the healthiest ways which can get you over your ex in 1 month: Don‘t jump into another relationship before you can emotionally commit to someone other than your ex. Because: I.e. people who get so desperate that they use others as a rebound, a bandaid and temporary distraction usually end up attracting people who will do the same to them down the line. So if you want an amazing long-term relationship that’s non-toxic, healthy, stable, based on mutual respect and authenticity, you got to engage in healthy behaviors, have higher standards for yourself than rebound relationships and simply not use others as an emotional bandaid. You got to become a person who heals in solitude and can be single for more than 6 months. Go no contact if you’re not legally bound to them and don’t have children. Keep contact at an absolute minimum if you can’t just cut the ties. Because none of us is immune to the workings of the subconscious mind. Meaning that you’re not the exception to the rule and need this distance and space in order to heal as much as everyone else needs it after a breakup. Reject their offer friendship, especially when there’s unrequited love involved. Because when you agree to your exes offer friendship (which is more often than not merely a way to soften the blow for themselves), they will: To save yourself these unnecessary mistakes, don’t stay friends with an ex you still love and with whom you want more than something platonic. You‘ll only be sabotaging yourself. Reject their offer for friendship instead and then decide to put yourself first, heal, accept that whatever you had is over and rediscover life without them. Block, unfollow and delete them on all social media. Because you wont ever find anything good on their social media profile. It will either be pictures of them being happy worh their new girlfriend/boyfriend or them posting baits to string you along and manipulate you into believing there’s still hope. By blocking, deleting and unfollowing them everywhere (and also deleting the fake profiles you use to cyberstalk them), you remove many of the obstacles that prolong your healing process and would otherwise keep you stuck for much longer than necessary. Own yor chunk that contributed to the breakup. It may just be 10% on you and 90% on them bur, that 10% is the only thing you can change, improve and control. The other 90% is completely outside your control and entirely on your ex to take care of. Doing this ensures you actually evolve and grow through the experience of this breakup, become more attractive and build better relationships as a byproduct of that.
